boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around ECU and Greenville.

cards.title: Browse the Gray Gallery
cards.subtitle: Jenkins Fine Arts Center, ECU
cards.notes: Walk through the current exhibition in Jenkins Fine Arts Center, then check the gallery page before you go for holiday closures.
cards.short_summary: A free ECU gallery visit with changing art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU states that the Wellington B. Gray Gallery is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: The Wellington B. Gray Gallery | School of Art & Design | ECU
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed for university holidays according to ECU.

cards.title: See work in the Senior Gallery
cards.subtitle: Jenkins Fine Arts Center, ECU
cards.notes: Stop into the Burroughs Wellcome Senior Gallery while visiting Jenkins and use the Gray Gallery page to confirm the current display.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery stop inside ECU’s Jenkins Fine Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU lists the Burroughs Wellcome Senior Gallery with the free, open-to-all Gray Gallery spaces.
cards.source_title: The Wellington B. Gray Gallery | School of Art & Design | ECU
cards.access_notes: ECU lists Monday–Friday hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m. and university-holiday closures for the galleries.

cards.entity_name: ECU Visiting Artists, Designers, and Scholars
cards.title: Attend a visiting artist talk
cards.subtitle: School of Art & Design, ECU
cards.notes: Check the School of Art & Design calendar for a visiting artist, designer, or scholar talk and arrive early enough to settle in.
cards.short_summary: School of Art & Design talks that are free and open to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU says its Visiting Artists, Designers, and Scholars events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visiting Artists, Designers, and Scholars | School of Art & Design | ECU
cards.access_notes: Events vary by the School of Art & Design calendar; ECU identifies them as free and open to the public.

cards.title: Claim a Joyner study room
cards.subtitle: Joyner Library, ECU main campus
cards.notes: Reserve a small or group room for a conversation, game plan, or quiet work session; use it only within the room’s listed limits.
cards.short_summary: Bookable library rooms for small groups or solo work.
cards.evidence_claim: Joyner Library provides reservable small and group study rooms for patrons, with first-come use when unreserved.
cards.source_title: Joyner Library Room Reservations
cards.access_notes: Small rooms support 1–2 people; group rooms support 2–6 people. Reservation availability and eligibility apply.

cards.title: Browse a Joyner exhibition
cards.subtitle: Joyner Library, ECU main campus
cards.notes: Make a loop through Joyner’s changing displays of photographs, maps, rare books, artifacts, and community art before settling elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: Rotating exhibits drawn from ECU collections and community art.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU says Joyner Library hosts exhibitions and displays of historical documents, photographs, rare books, maps, artwork, and artifacts.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | Joyner Library | ECU
cards.access_notes: Located inside Joyner Library; check library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the campus one-mile route
cards.subtitle: ECU main campus
cards.notes: Use ECU Recreation & Wellness’s Campus 1 Mile route PDF for an easy, self-paced loop with a friend between classes.
cards.short_summary: A mapped one-mile campus walk from ECU Recreation & Wellness.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU Recreation & Wellness publishes a Campus 1 Mile walking route.
cards.source_title: Walking Routes | Campus Recreation & Wellness | ECU
cards.access_notes: This is a self-guided outdoor route; follow campus pedestrian rules and weather conditions.

cards.title: Take the North Rec walk/jog loop
cards.subtitle: North Recreational Complex, ECU
cards.notes: Download ECU’s North Rec Walk/Jog route, bring water, and use the marked route for a low-key outdoor catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A published ECU walk/jog route at North Rec.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU Recreation & Wellness lists a North Rec Walk/Jog route among its walking routes.
cards.source_title: Walking Routes | Campus Recreation & Wellness | ECU
cards.access_notes: This is a self-guided outdoor route; follow posted complex rules and use it during appropriate daylight conditions.

cards.title: Walk Town Common’s riverfront
cards.subtitle: 105 E. 1st St., Greenville
cards.notes: Meet by the Tar River esplanade, take the paved walkway, and pause at the benches or playground area without reserving a shelter.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront public park with greenway and paved walking space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Greenville lists Town Common amenities including a greenway, walking trails, paved walkway, benches, and public restrooms.
cards.source_title: Town Common | City of Greenville
cards.access_notes: Public park amenities are available without a shelter reservation; reservations apply only to reserved facilities.

cards.title: Visit the Greenville Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 802 South Evans St., Greenville
cards.notes: Browse the galleries on your own, and skip the paid guided tour if you want to keep the visit entirely free.
cards.short_summary: Free general admission to a Greenville art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville Museum of Art states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit GMOA | Greenville Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; the museum lists Tuesday–Saturday hours, 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Paid guided tours are optional.

cards.title: Stroll the Pitt County Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 403 Government Circle, Greenville
cards.notes: Take a self-guided walk through the garden collections, or register ahead for a scheduled plant walk when one fits your calendar.
cards.short_summary: A public garden with no admission charge and free parking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pitt County Arboretum states that there is no admission charge and that parking is free.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | The Pitt County Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public seven days a week from dawn to dusk; seasonal detailed hours are listed by the arboretum.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Uptown and Dickinson Avenue destinations in Greenville, the downtown area directly beside ECU’s main campus.

cards.title: Greenville Town Common
cards.subtitle: East 1st Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Walk the paved riverwalk and green space at this 21-acre Town Common, then check the venue calendar if you want to pair the stop with a public event.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront public-green-space stop beside Uptown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town Common has 21 acres of open green space, paved connections to the South Tar River Greenway, and a 1,500-foot riverwalk.
cards.source_title: Greenville Town Common | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: Located at 105 East 1st Street; event programming varies.

cards.title: Greenville Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Use the museum’s exhibit schedule to choose a visit, and allow time to look through both the permanent collection and any traveling exhibition on view.
cards.short_summary: A named Evans Street museum with permanent and traveling art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville Museum of Art presents 19th- and 20th-century American art from its permanent collection alongside traveling exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Greenville Museum of Art | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 802 South Evans Street; classes, workshops, and events may have separate requirements.

cards.title: Emerge Gallery and Art Center
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Check the rotating gallery program before you go, or look for an age-appropriate class or workshop offered by the Pitt County Arts Council.
cards.short_summary: A downtown arts center with two changing galleries and creative programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerge is home to the Pitt County Arts Council and has two galleries with rotating exhibits, a sales gallery, and classes and workshops.
cards.source_title: Emerge Gallery and Art Center | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 404 South Evans Street; workshop enrollment and exhibition access may vary.

cards.title: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery
cards.subtitle: Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Use this named Evans Street coffee-and-creamery stop as a daytime anchor while walking between Uptown destinations; confirm menu and seating directly before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A coffee house and creamery on the central Uptown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery is located at 431 Evans Street in Greenville.
cards.source_title: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 431 Evans Street; purchases are required for food or drinks.

cards.title: Emerald City Collective
cards.subtitle: East 4th Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Look for current pop-up or gallery details before heading over, especially during the First Friday ArtWalk season when the space hosts participating artists.
cards.short_summary: A downtown gallery and pop-up shop that participates in First Friday ArtWalk.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerald City Collective is a gallery and pop-up shop at 106 East 4th Street and participates in Downtown Greenville First Friday ArtWalks from September through June.
cards.source_title: Emerald City Collective | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 106 East 4th Street; pop-up and ArtWalk participation are seasonal or event-specific.

cards.title: Greenville-Pitt County Visitors Center
cards.subtitle: Cotanche Street corridor, Downtown Greenville
cards.notes: Start here to pick up local orientation help, then use the nearby garage or surface lots if you are arriving by car for an Uptown walk.
cards.short_summary: A Cotanche Street visitor-information stop across from the Fourth Street garage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville-Pitt County Convention & Visitors Bureau operates its Visitors Center at 417 Cotanche Street, Suite 100, across from the Fourth Street Parking Garage.
cards.source_title: Visitors Center | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 417 Cotanche Street, Suite 100; the visitor center lists Monday–Friday daytime service.

cards.title: The Martinsborough
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Pause outside to photograph the restored Jefferson Blount-Harvey Building, then consult the venue’s calendar if you are considering an event-based visit.
cards.short_summary: A restored 1923 building used as a downtown special-events venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Martinsborough occupies the restored Jefferson Blount-Harvey Building, built in 1923, and serves as a venue for special events and receptions.
cards.source_title: The Martinsborough | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 330 South Evans Street; access depends on private or scheduled events.

cards.title: Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor, Dickinson Avenue District
cards.notes: Browse the indoor market’s seasonal vendor mix in the former bottling plant, and check current vendors or hours before making the walk from campus.
cards.short_summary: An indoor, year-round market in a former Cher-Cola bottling plant.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market is an indoor, year-round market in a 100-year-old former Cher-Cola bottling plant featuring items made or grown within 50 miles of Greenville.
cards.source_title: Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 716 Dickinson Avenue; purchases are optional and vendor offerings vary.

cards.title: The Greenville Metal Zoo
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor at 9th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street area to view the repurposed-metal sculptures, then keep an eye out for additional works around Downtown businesses.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sculpture stop centered at Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville Metal Zoo is an outdoor sculpture park of repurposed-metal works by artist Jonathan Bowling, centered at Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street.
cards.source_title: The Greenville Metal Zoo | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are described at the Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street intersection and elsewhere downtown.

cards.title: Native Fine Diner
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor, Dickinson Avenue Historic District
cards.notes: Use the former Carolina Grill Diner building as a documented Dickinson Avenue landmark, and check the restaurant directly for current service details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A restored former diner building in the Dickinson Avenue Historic District.
cards.evidence_claim: Native Fine Diner is at 907 Dickinson Avenue in the restored location of Greenville’s former Carolina Grill Diner, within the Historic Dickinson Avenue Arts District.
cards.source_title: Native Fine Diner | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 907 Dickinson Avenue; purchases are required for restaurant offerings.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented ECU rituals, campus legends and recurring celebrations, including one tradition that concluded in 2026.

cards.title: Wait Until Graduation to Walk Under the Cupola
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Mall
cards.notes: Pause at the Cupola for a photo, then take the surrounding paths until graduation if you want to follow ECU’s four-year superstition.
cards.short_summary: A campus legend says passing beneath the Cupola before graduating delays a four-year graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU describes the Cupola as a campus tradition and says legend holds that students who walk under it before graduating will not graduate in four years.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark on the Main Campus Mall; follow campus access guidance.

cards.title: Make the No Quarter Cross in the Fourth
cards.subtitle: ECU athletic events
cards.notes: At an ECU game, watch for the fourth-quarter No Quarter moment and join the approved crowd gesture only when the game presentation cues it.
cards.short_summary: The red No Quarter flag and crossed-arm gesture signal ECU’s late-game Pirate identity.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU states that, when entering the fourth quarter, students raise their arms in a cross and cheer ECU teams onward to victory as part of No Quarter.
cards.source_title: Trademarks | Licensing | ECU
cards.access_notes: Occurs during athletic events; game admission or ticket requirements may apply.

cards.title: Ring In, Then Ring Out
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Student Center entrance
cards.notes: Find the Boneyard Bell by the Main Campus Student Center entrance and ring it at an arrival or graduation milestone, as its plaque invites.
cards.short_summary: SGA’s recommissioned bell marks the beginning and ending of a student’s ECU journey.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU SGA says incoming students ring the Boneyard Bell when they arrive and graduating students ring it as they leave their alma mater.
cards.source_title: Boneyard Bell | Student Government Association | ECU
cards.access_notes: Located at the main entrance of the Main Campus Student Center; observe any event or building access rules.

cards.title: Close Spring Classes at Barefoot on the Mall
cards.subtitle: ECU Mall
cards.notes: Check the Student Activities Board’s spring programming and attend the Mall celebration on the final day of classes before exams begin.
cards.short_summary: Since 1979, ECU has used this annual event to mark the end of spring-semester classes.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU reports that Barefoot on the Mall began in 1979, is held on the last day of spring classes, and is hosted annually by the Student Activities Board.
cards.source_title: Barefoot on the Mall celebrates end of academic year | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Annual spring-semester event; consult ECU’s current event details for attendance information.

cards.title: Remember the Polar Bear Plunge
cards.subtitle: Eakin Student Recreation Center outdoor pool
cards.notes: Treat this as ECU history: the 30th and final plunge was scheduled for January 2026, closing a tradition that began in 1997.
cards.short_summary: A cold-weather pool-jump tradition ran for 30 years before ECU announced its final event.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU reported that the 30th and final Polar Bear Plunge was planned for January 2026 and that the first event occurred in January 1997.
cards.source_title: Final Polar Bear Plunge reflects campus tradition | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Discontinued after its final 2026 event; do not attempt an unsupervised pool jump.

cards.title: Start the Year at Pirate Palooza
cards.subtitle: Pirate Weeks of Welcome
cards.notes: Look for Pirate Palooza in the fall welcome schedule and use it to sample activities, games and campus organizations with new classmates.
cards.short_summary: ECU’s large welcome-back gathering is part of the opening rhythm of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU News Services identifies Pirate Palooza as an ECU tradition and ECU’s largest welcome-back event.
cards.source_title: New Crew | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Typically associated with fall welcome programming; verify the current year’s schedule and location.

cards.title: Answer “Purple!” With “Gold!”
cards.subtitle: ECU campus and athletic culture
cards.notes: Learn the short Purple–Gold call-and-response during orientation, then use it when it is led at ECU gatherings or athletic events.
cards.short_summary: The school-color chant is introduced to new Pirates as part of ECU campus culture.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s orientation guidance tells incoming students to learn the “Purple! Gold!” chant as part of campus culture.
cards.source_title: Summer Orientation | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Used at university gatherings and games; participate when led by event staff or performers.

cards.title: Learn “E.C. Victory” Before Game Day
cards.subtitle: ECU athletic events
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a game and follow the band, cheer squad or videoboard so you can join the song at the right time.
cards.short_summary: ECU identifies its fight song as an essential Pirate tradition to learn.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s admissions tradition guide names “E.C. Victory” as the university fight song and calls the fight song essential to learn.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Commonly heard at athletic events; game admission or ticket requirements may apply.

cards.title: Keep the Alma Mater in the Rotation
cards.subtitle: University ceremonies and ECU gatherings
cards.notes: Save the official Alma Mater lyrics and listen for it at ECU ceremonies or gatherings, where it connects current students with alumni.
cards.short_summary: The Alma Mater is one of the songs ECU explicitly asks Pirates to know.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s admissions tradition guide presents the East Carolina University Alma Mater and calls the alma mater essential to learn.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial use varies by event; follow the program and event staff directions.

cards.title: Spot the Trustees Mace at Commencement
cards.subtitle: ECU graduation ceremonies
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the handcrafted Trustees Mace in the formal procession and read its history as part of ECU’s ceremonial tradition.
cards.short_summary: A specially commissioned ceremonial mace became an early symbolic tradition at ECU.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU News Services reports that the Trustees Mace was commissioned before the 1978 chancellor installation and was among ECU’s first symbolic traditions.
cards.source_title: ECU uses ancient symbol in graduation ceremony | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Appears in formal university ceremonies; attendance and guest policies vary by ceremony.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at East Carolina University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of named campus and Greenville stops for getting oriented, meeting people, and choosing a weekend activity.

cards.title: Begin at the Main Campus Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · orientation and campus services
cards.notes: Use the first-floor public areas as a meeting point, then check posted student programming or ask the desk where the day’s activities are happening.
cards.short_summary: A central starting point with inclusive student spaces and dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU describes the Main Campus Student Center as offering inclusive, engaging spaces for student life and well-being, with multiple dining options.
cards.source_title: Main Campus Student Center | Student Centers | ECU
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Centers hours page before visiting; building access and programming vary by date.

cards.title: Take a first campus photo at the ECU Letters
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · outside the Main Campus Student Center
cards.notes: Walk outside the Main Campus Student Center for a quick group-photo stop, then use the campus map to choose the next nearby destination.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark beside the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU identifies the bold ECU letters outside the Main Campus Student Center as a campus landmark and photo spot.
cards.source_title: Iconic Pirate History | Student Academic Success Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use the ECU campus map for current wayfinding.

cards.title: Cross Campus Mall and get your bearings
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main Campus pedestrian route
cards.notes: Make this your walking connector: pause to orient yourself on the interactive map, identify classrooms, and pick a route toward Joyner Library.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed Main Campus landmark that works as a natural walking pause.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s interactive campus map lists Campus Mall as a named Main Campus location.
cards.source_title: ECU Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; consult the interactive map for accessibility and construction updates.

cards.title: Make Joyner Library your weekend reset point
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · Main Campus Library
cards.notes: Stop by the circulation or research desk to learn the building layout, then choose a quiet place to plan the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: ECU’s main-campus library offers research help and a staffed service desk.
cards.evidence_claim: Joyner Library provides Ask a Librarian and subject-specialist liaison services; ECU publishes current Main Campus Library hours online.
cards.source_title: ECU Libraries Hours - Building Hours
cards.access_notes: Current building hours are posted by ECU and change by term; verify them before going.

cards.title: Plan a meal at West End Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · West Campus dining stop
cards.notes: Review the dining page and your meal-plan options before heading over, then use dinner as an easy way to reconnect with new classmates.
cards.short_summary: A named ECU dining hall used in new-student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s 2026 orientation schedule places student dinner at West End Dining Hall, and ECU Dining maintains a dedicated West End location page.
cards.source_title: West End Dining Hall - ECU Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Menus and hours are published by ECU Dining; check the location page on the day because schedules can change.

cards.title: Walk by Trustees Fountain after dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Wright Circle
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a brief outdoor pause on your way across campus; read the nearby trustee inscriptions and continue toward Wright Auditorium.
cards.short_summary: A named Wright Circle landmark with documented ECU history.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU reports that Trustees Fountain in Wright Circle was dedicated in 2009, replacing the earlier Wright Fountain at the site.
cards.source_title: Trustees Fountain dedicated | ECU News Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark near Wright Auditorium; observe from public walkways.

cards.title: Check Wright Auditorium’s current calendar
cards.subtitle: Friday night · 212 Wright Circle
cards.notes: Look for a performance that fits your weekend and confirm ticket or entry details before you go; the venue’s events include music, theatre, and dance.
cards.short_summary: A historic multi-use campus venue with an active event calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU says Wright Auditorium hosts symphonies, plays, concerts, and dance performances throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Wright Auditorium - East Carolina University
cards.access_notes: Events and admission requirements vary; ECU lists the venue at 212 Wright Circle and directs visitors to event-specific information.

cards.entity_name: Richard R. and JoAnn M. Eakin Student Recreation Center
cards.title: Try one activity at Eakin Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Campus Recreation & Wellness
cards.notes: Bring the required ECU credentials and choose one approachable activity, such as a basketball court, indoor track, pool, or climbing wall session.
cards.short_summary: A large ECU recreation facility with varied indoor activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU states that the Eakin Student Recreation Center has basketball courts, a climbing wall, indoor and outdoor pools, fitness areas, and an indoor track.
cards.source_title: Richard R. and JoAnn M. Eakin Student Recreation Center | Campus Recreation & Wellness | ECU
cards.access_notes: Facility use may require student eligibility and hours vary; verify Campus Recreation & Wellness access rules before arrival.

cards.title: Make an outdoor plan at North Recreational Complex
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · about 10 minutes from Main Campus by car
cards.notes: Coordinate transportation before leaving campus, then choose a daytime activity around the multipurpose fields, water, or sand beach within posted rules.
cards.short_summary: An ECU recreation area with fields, water, and a sand beach.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU says the North Recreational Complex has eight multipurpose fields, six acres of water for boating and fishing, a sand beach, and is about a 10-minute drive from Main Campus.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation & Wellness | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Arrange transportation and confirm current facility access, equipment, and water-activity rules with Campus Recreation & Wellness.

cards.title: Close the weekend at Greenville Town Common
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · 105 East First Street, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk on the paved connections by the Tar River, visit the Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza, and check the city calendar for all-ages programs.
cards.short_summary: Greenville’s central park connects to the Tar River Greenway and Uptown.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Greenville identifies Town Common as its central park, with 21 acres, Tar River Greenway connections, a river walk, and Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza.
cards.source_title: Greenville Town Common | City of Greenville, NC
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; use daylight judgment and consult the city page for programmed events or recreation updates.
